neighbours.label: the line break that ends a line of a fiction scene, as opposed to line breaks in news or instructions and to the same kind of scene run together with no line breaks
fire:
"You lied to me," Clara said. She stepped back from the window and folded her arms.
"I had to," he said.
"No, you didn't."
He looked down at his hands. She waited.
"I'm sorry," he whispered.
She turned away.
Marcus leaned against the doorframe and watched her pack. Neither of them spoke for a while.
"Where will you go?" he asked.
She shrugged.
"Anywhere but here."
He turned slowly and looked away.
Nora dropped her keys on the counter and kicked off her shoes.
"You're late," Ethan said from the couch.
"I know."
She poured herself a glass of water and drank it slowly.
He was still watching her.
"Are we going to talk about it?"
The rain had stopped by the time they reached the car. Lena felt for her keys.
"Let me drive," Tom said.
She glanced at him and sighed.
"You've been drinking."
He held up his hands and stepped back.
Isabel closed the book and looked up at her sister. The room had gone very quiet.
"Did he tell you?"
Anna shook her head.
"He didn't have to."
Isabel bit her lip and said nothing.
He found her on the back steps with a blanket around her shoulders.
"You should come inside," he said.
She didn't look up.
"In a minute."
He sat down beside her and waited.
After a while she leaned against him.
"Who sent you?" Rourke asked. His voice was low and his hand had not left his belt.
The boy swallowed.
"Nobody, sir."
Rourke studied him for a long moment.
"Try again," he said.
The boy looked at the floor.
Sophie set the two mugs on the table and pulled out a chair.
"So," she said. "How bad is it?"
Daniel rubbed his eyes.
"Bad."
She reached across and touched his wrist.
He almost smiled.
quiet:
The school board met on Thursday to review next year's budget. Parents spoke for an hour.
"We need more teachers," one parent said.
The board voted four to three.
The budget goes to the city in May.
A final vote is expected in June.

To replace the filter, turn off the water at the main valve. Wait one minute.
Unscrew the old filter.
Push the new one into place.
Turn the water back on.
Check the joint for leaks.

Police said a man was arrested on Friday after a fire at a warehouse on Mill Road.
"Nobody was hurt," a spokesman said.
The building was empty at the time.
The road reopened on Saturday.
An inquiry has begun.

The museum opens at ten every day except Monday. Tickets can be bought at the door.
Children under five enter free.
The cafe closes at four.
Guided tours start at noon.
Large bags must be left in the cloakroom.

"You lied to her," Maria said. She stepped back from the table and folded her arms. "I had to," he said. "No, you didn't." He looked down at his boots. She waited. "I'm sorry," he whispered. She turned away and walked out.

Peter leaned against the railing and watched her leave. Neither of them spoke for a while. "Where will you go?" he asked. She shrugged. "Anywhere but here." He turned slowly and looked away toward the water.

Julia dropped her bag on the bench and took off her gloves. "You're late," Owen said from the stove. "I know." She poured herself a cup of tea and drank it slowly. He was still watching her. "Are we going to talk about it?"

He found her in the garden with a coat around her shoulders. "You should come inside," he said. She didn't look up. "In a minute." He sat down beside her and waited. After a while she leaned against him and closed her eyes.
